source_refs.note: Topic 7.2 with the Class Activity and example (PDF 94-95); no book figure. The hypotheses figure is original and the two types are carried as a table. Short Q3, Long Q2 and MCQs 2-3 are answered here. The check question is added.

blocks.text: Hypotheses are of different types, each with its own purpose. The two most common, the null and the alternative hypothesis, work together in every test, and correct hypotheses reduce confusion and improve the analysis.

blocks.caption: Null and alternative hypotheses
rows: No effect, difference or relationship (the default assumption)
There is an effect, difference or relationship (the opposite of H0)
The data is tested against it; it is rejected only if the evidence against it is strong. It gives a neutral base for comparison and helps avoid bias.
What the research usually hopes to support; it represents change or impact, and needs strong evidence.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Write a null and an alternative hypothesis for a situation about marks or percentages, and discuss whether they are correct.

items: Research question: Does the amount of study time affect students' exam scores?
H0: There is no significant relationship between study time and exam scores.
H1: The amount of study time significantly affects students' exam scores.
Clear and specific: vague statements reduce accuracy.
Testable with data, with variables clearly defined.

blocks.text: Correctly formulated hypotheses save time and lead to reliable results.
